summary: At step 33, the second #jump command has identical C and JavaScript screens and all 4126 RNG calls, but C leaves the prompt cursor at the hero [43,8] while JavaScript leaves it at [45,10]. The actionable ordering defect is that C apply.c calls getpos_sethilite() before entering getpos(); getpos() then runs handle_tip() and the verbose pline before its initial curs/flush_screen(0). Those C messages flush the forced selection with cursor_on_u=1, consuming the dirty glyphs and returning the cursor to the hero. JS getpos.js runs handle_tip/verbose ttyPline first, then forceGetposSelectionRedraw() marks the selection and manually restores to its maximum [45,10].

source.branch: During a physical Knight #jump, C apply.c:2058-2063 prints the jump prompt, installs getpos_sethilite(display_jump_positions, get_valid_jump_position), and enters getpos(). C getpos.c:838-847 then handles the one-time GETPOS tip and verbose pline before :848-854 calls curs/flush_screen(0). The callback change has already marked the valid selection, so pline.c:273-274 flushes it with cursor_on_u=1 and leaves the cursor on the hero before getpos's zero-mode flush. JS apply.js installs callback fields, but JS getpos.js:904 and :918 performs handle_tip/verbose ttyPline before :924 forceGetposSelectionRedraw(); the forced selection is therefore marked after the pre-cursor flush and :927-932 moves to its selected maximum, producing [45,10] instead of C [43,8] while screens and RNG remain equal.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2058-2064 jump() installs display_jump_positions/get_valid_jump_position and calls getpos(&cc, TRUE, ...); this is the recorded #jump production entry.
js/apply.js:1139-1151 jump() installs state.getpos_hilitefunc/state.getpos_getvalid and calls getpos(target, true, ...), then clears the callback state in its finally block.

nethack-c/upstream/src/getpos.c:848-854 getpos() initializes the target cursor and calls flush_screen(0); :1151-1165 exits through getpos_sethilite(NULL, NULL), preserving the source callback lifetime and dirty-buffer transition.
js/getpos.js:200-224 forceGetposSelectionRedraw() and :921-932 getpos() implement the current full-scan and speculative cursor restoration that diverge from the C TTY behavior.
dependencies: nethack-c/upstream/src/selvar.c:802-810 selection_force_newsyms() walks the selection in source order and calls newsym_force() only for selected points.

nethack-c/upstream/src/display.c:1863-1871 newsym_force() updates gbuf_start/gbuf_stop and gnew; :2208-2266 flush_screen(0) prints only pending ranges, while pline.c:273-274 invokes flush_screen(1) for the pre-cursor messages and explicitly returns the cursor to u.ux/u.uy.

js/display.js:5933-6020 flush_screen() already preserves the cursor around complete-grid rebuilding; the actionable JS defect is that forceGetposSelectionRedraw() runs after the equivalent pre-cursor ttyPline calls instead of modeling the C callback's earlier dirty-selection installation.

nethack-c/upstream/src/getpos.c:41-63 installs the callback and calls selection_force_newsyms() before getpos's own body; :838-847 then runs handle_tip/verbose output before :848-854's curs/flush_screen(0). nethack-c/upstream/src/pline.c:273-274 proves those messages flush with cursor_on_u=1, so the forced selection is consumed and the hero cursor is expected before getpos begins input.

nethack-c/upstream/src/selvar.c:802-810 and display.c:1863-1871/2208-2266 establish the dirty-selection transition, but the assigned mismatch does not require a general sparse-range cursor model: the source-order preflush already explains why C has [43,8] at step 33.

The refined implementation scope is this getpos selection-install/initial-flush ordering, with js/apply.js jump() as the production caller to verify; no gameplay, RNG, or broad renderer correction is indicated.
